lines.en: Something was happening inside of the Kumon-mi Mall.
They say it’s “renovations.” But if you check online, they don’t ever tell you what they’re renovating. And that makes me immensely distrustful.
Other things that make me immensely distrustful are the virality of fake animal rescue videos, pricing that ends with .99, and the unfortunate fact that I am always being lied to.
I want to see what’s being built inside of those walls. I want to know what’s happening above and below. Where that massive hole leads to. How the town still breathes.
And something tells me that soon, I will.
Because Tsubasa Tsukioka has special privileges and is allowed inside during the construction for some reason.
How convenient that I get to stick to her today!
: This was a fuckin’ horrible idea, Nee-sama!
Oh, it looks like she’s allowed to bring a friend too.
: Because of the price tag, I assume? You needn’t worry about that. Whatever you want is on me.
: Not because of the fuckin’ price tag! Because I look like a god damn Barbie and the only experience I have with those is rippin’ their heads off and setting ‘em on fire!
: Why do all poor people seem to have the most morbid ideas of how to have fun? I don’t even want to think of what you’d have done to that poor doll’s dream house.
: That shit was for rich kids. But I’d have probably set that on fire too.
: I’m sure you look fine, Yuki. Just open the curtain if you’re unsure and I’ll gladly weigh in. No one else is here if you’re worried about being seen.
: I am worried about being seen, but only cause I ain’t ever gonna be able to live this down.
: You’re only saying that because you have no confidence, darling. I’m sure you’re stunning. Now, go on — peel back the curtain. Show me the dress.
: Ugh. Fine.
: I fucking hate you.
: HA!
: Okay. Fun’s over. I’m puttin’ real clothes back on.
: You look like a failed makeover scene from a John Hughes film! Or like you fell into the bargain bin of a Beverly Hills Goodwill! I love it! Come back! I need to take photos!
: You’re lucky I’m dying! I’d never let anybody fuck with me like this under normal circumstances!
: Oh, can it. If I wanted to “fuck” with you, I’d parade you around town wearing that. If anything, you’re lucky that I want this moment all to myself.
: Yeah. Real lucky you get to burn that image into your mind while I try to figure out how to take this damn thing off. Look like a goddamn bride right now.
: Savor it while you can, then. It’s not like you’ll ever get married, so you may want to burn this image into your memory as well.
: I AM married!
: I meant to a real man — not one who sits idly by while his wife is violated by a group of cronies who I may or may not have had subsequently castrated.
: You did what?
: Hm? I didn’t say anything.
: The fuck were you doin’ over there anyway? Thought you hated the Yakuza. Some kinda business thing?
: Something like that. Can we not just say I was searching for a damsel in distress?
: You can, I guess. Just it’d make you look bad since you took your sweet ass time finding me.
: Mmm, and whose fault is it that I needed to find you in the first place? Hmm?
: I don’t know what you’re talkin’ about. We done here?
: Already? But we haven’t gotten our nails done yet.
: By who? You took me to a fuckin’ mall without any people in it. I don’t know how to paint my own nails.
: Even better! I’ll do them for you! Here-
: N-Nee-sama! Leave my fuckin’ hands alone-
: Oh my. Do you always bite them like this? They look absolutely horrendous.
: Get your fuckin’ hands off of me!
: I swear, Yuki — you put up a stronger fight against me than you do when you’re being gang-raped.
: I am in much better shape now. You try puttin’ up a fight when the only things you’ve put in your body for a week straight are drugs and alcohol.
: Impossible. I know better than to treat my body in such a way. And you would too if you were not such a brat all the time.
: Ain’t nobody ever called me that and lived to tell the tale, you know.
: In fact, ain’t nobody ever called me that in general, I don’t think.
: Good. Only I should be able to say mean things to you without being punished. This is my privilege as the most powerful woman in Kumon-mi.
: Oh, fuck off. Same shit was true before you even were the most powerful woman in Kumon-mi. You just enjoy makin’ my life difficult.
: Yes, but now I can make it even more difficult because I currently am the most powerful woman in Kumon-mi.
: Do you have any idea how easy it would be for me to have you locked up and forced to play dress-up with me forever?
: Why don’t you then if you get so much fuckin’ enjoyment out of it?
: The same reason as last time. A forest bird never wants a cage.
: What, you gonna get all poetic on me now? You know I ain’t good at that shit.
: I’m just saying — it’s your freedom that’s always made you so beautiful. Taking that away would be a sin that not even God can forgive.
: You know I ain’t about that God shit either, Nee-sama.
: Mm.
: And perhaps that’s for the best.
The two girls — or women as they were now — found their way to the parking lot where Yuki’s bike was left.
And before long they were off, bathed in the glow of the moon to the point where it felt as if there was a third person right there with them.
But there wasn’t. And there never would be again because that’s just how life works sometimes.
But even in those moments of sad acceptance, it’s always possible to find joy.
This was a very rare moment in which both of these girls — or women as they were forced to be — could feel that at once.
: You sure you want to ride with me instead of takin’ one of your fancy limos back? Just as reckless now as I was when we were kids, you know.
: I do hope you aren’t going to ask me that every single time. You did the same thing on the way here.
: Feel obligated to. Ain’t used to carryin’ precious cargo anymore. Might make me a little jumpy.
: How far do you think my old house is from here?
: You serious? Been stuck in that mansion for so long you can’t even remember where you’re from?
: I’m not stuck there. I’m a willing participant of my own seclusion. It makes moments like this all the more special.
: You sure you ain’t just brainwashed? I’ve heard money changes people, you know.
: Does it? Do I seem all that different to you then, Yuki?
: Nah. Still a pain in the ass. Still holdin’ on just as tight as ever.
: Only because I feel like you’ll leave me behind if I don’t.
: Don’t worry. It’s common courtesy to stop the bike if your passenger falls off.
: Right...
: That’s what I meant.
: Wait! The beach is the other way! You told me you were taking me swimming! I bought a new bikini for this and everything!
: Sorry, Nee-sama! New plan! Gonna have to deal with it!
: I knew it! I always knew you’d hold me ransom one day! Whatever you’re being offered, I’ll pay you double! Or...how...how much are you being offered exactly?
: Nadda.
: You’re doing it for free?! You delinquents are so dumb sometimes! You could make so much money off of me!
: Sounds kinda like you’re tryin’ to talk me into it.
: I’m just saying — if you’re going to kidnap someone, the least you can do is try to profit off of it. This is why I’m rich and you’re not.
: If I wanted to kidnap you, I’d have done it already. We’re just goin’ to the lake instead. Fewer people. Less of a chance that we’ll be caught. Figured you’d like that.
: The lake? You can swim in those? Aren’t they full of fish and bugs and trash and just...generally disgusting, small bodies of water?
: You know it. So you might want to leave that fancy new swimsuit in your bag and just jump in naked with the rest of us.
: You’re joking.
: Or you could stay on land. Makes no difference to me.
: You’d really have me sit there and watch a bunch of delinquents skinny-dip in a garbage-infested lake?
: Course not. I’d have you join us in that garbage-infested lake. You’re the one who’s being a priss about it.
: But what happens if something gross touches my leg?
: Then something gross touches your leg. The fuck you want me to do about it?
: Protect me, obviously! You know I don’t like gross things!
: That shit’s just part of life, Nee-sama. You’re gonna miss out on all of the fun if you’re constantly worried like that.
: Can you at least call me by name if you’re going to indoctrinate me into this filthy way of living? I’m tired of hearing you say “Nee-sama” all the time. It’s so uncharacteristic.
: Nah.
: You shot me down so easily!
: Just bein’ respectful, you know? You’re on a level I can’t ever even hope to reach.
: Huh? Why not?
: Just ain’t how shit works in the real world. Least not most of the time. You were born to eat from silver spoons and shit and I was born to polish ‘em.
: Ain’t really a bad thing, though. I like livin’ this way. Havin’ nobody who expects anything from me and nobody who feels like they’ve gotta look for me when I go missing.
: Just different worlds we’ve got. And if you really wanna see mine, you’re gonna have to be a little more open. Capiche?
: Va bene.
: What?
: Oh. Sorry. I assumed you spoke Italian.
: Why?
: Because...you said “capiche.” That’s Italian.
: Oh, no shit? Had no clue. The fuck’s “va bene” then?
: It means, like...fine. Or okay. I was submitting to your demands and agreeing to get naked and jump into a lake with you and all of your delinquent friends.
: Atta girl. Proud of you, Nee-sama.
: I don’t want them staring at me, though. I’ve never been nude in front of anyone before. Let alone in a garbage-infested lake.
: Roger that. I’ll make sure everyone but you spends the entire day with their eyes closed. This is a completely reasonable demand.
: I don’t mind if you see me.
: You say something back there? Couldn’t hear you over the-
: Nope. Nothing at all.
: Just as warm as I remember...
: You say something back there? Couldn’t hear you over the-
: Hey, it’s not too late to stop by the lake, is it?
: Which lake? The fuck you wanna do that for?
: Just a spontaneous decision. No reason for it, really.
: Mind if we take a rain check then? Told Sara I’d clean the bar for her tomorrow morning.
: I can just hire someone to clean it for you instead. A whole team, perhaps. She wouldn’t need to pay a dime and it’d be much faster.
: No can do, Nee-sama. This ain’t about money. It’s about tryin’ to get back to where I was before everything went to hell. Means I’ve gotta be “responsible” and shit.
: Of course...If that’s what you feel you need to do, I have no right to try and hold you back.
: You good back there? Seem a little...quieter all of a sudden.
: Just a little nostalgic is all. I missed this.
: Yeah — cause gettin’ dragged around by some delinquent on a bike was way better than whatever the fuck you were doin’ in your ivory tower.
: Would you have been happy if you were stuck in that tower with me, Yuki?
: I am now. And it ain’t been that bad so far. Not a fan of that fancy shit you keep making me eat, though. Not sure how you do it.
: Then why don’t we stop somewhere cheap for dinner so you’re not forced to eat anything fancy again?
: Now you’re speakin’ my language. Have anythin’ in mind?
: Hmm...
: Have you ever heard of “tacos?”
: What?
: They’re a Mexican dish that-
: I know what a fuckin’ taco is, Nee-sama. Just wasn’t expectin’ to hear that from a princess like you.
: Oh, splendid! Then, take us to the subway. I know a place where we can get them.
: Subway tacos. This has gotta be the least boujee thing you’ve ever suggested.
: It’s the least I can do after making you wear that dress.
: Heh. It’s always gotta be a fuckin’ trade with you. Hold on tight, okay?
: This is why I’m rich and you’re- ahh! Yuki?!?! This speed...can’t be legal!
: It’s not! But it’s fun as hell, ain’t it?!
Perhaps it was a good thing that the only one who could see them was the moon, for Tsubasa Tsukioka had a difficult time being herself in front of anyone else.
And for a while, it felt to her as if she’d never get to be that again.
It came with a tinge of guilt, though — for she’d opened the door of a cage she bought in hopes that a forest bird would fly into it on its own.
That she’d be content watching it grow fat under her supervision and thrive in false captivity.
But she was the one who filled that cage with berries and seeds, so it all still felt a little forced. Like it was only there to eat.
But perhaps if she kept waiting, it would one day land on her shoulder.
The thought of that alone was enough to keep her going when all else began to crumble.
